Subject: Solstice request — architecture and isolation evidence for SIG questionnaire

Marcus,

Thanks for taking this on. Solstice's InfoSec team is working through a SIG questionnaire for our board review and we need a concise set of artifacts describing Redwood's network & tenancy isolation for Dedicated and Private deployments. Specifically we need:

- A short (1–2 page) narrative describing the isolation model for Dedicated vs Private (control plane boundaries, tenant data paths, management plane access).
- High-level network diagrams (PNG/SVG) that show the separation between control plane, management plane, tenant compute, and any inbound/outbound egress flows.
- A table listing per-tenant segmentation controls (ACLs, security groups, route tables, microsegmentation controls).
- Evidence examples: a sample audit log entry showing access to tenant KV store, a sample KMS/HSM integration note, and the egress policy matrix.

Timing: can you provide these artifacts by EOD June 11? If you prefer, we can set a 30-min walkthrough next week.

Background: Solstice is evaluating Redwood Dedicated + Private for a regulated deployment (clinical trial data, some datasets subject to regional retention rules). The SIG responses will determine scope of our procurement.

Thanks,

--

Subject: Re: Solstice request — architecture and isolation evidence for SIG questionnaire

Emma —

Appreciate the clear ask. We've assembled an initial package that covers the items you listed; attaching the first-pass artifacts and a proposed delivery plan. Highlights below, full details are in the attachments.

Key points (short form):
- Isolation model: Dedicated pools provide hardware-segregated GPU pools with tenant scheduling constrained to reserved instances and network-layer segmentation (separate VPCs or VNets). Private deployments run the same runtime but packaged with a customer-controlled control plane; we maintain an optional thin control plane agent that can be air-gapped per contract.
- Control plane boundaries: Management/control plane traffic uses a distinct, authenticated channel (mTLS + per-cluster certs) between customer-managed control plane endpoints and our orchestration agents. No tenant inference data flows into Redwood's control plane for Private deployments unless explicitly enabled.
- Data paths: Tenant inference traffic is pinned to tenant compute nodes; prefix/KV cache is logically scoped per-tenant with optional physical isolation for Dedicated customers.
- KMS & keys: We support customer-managed keys via KMS or HSMs (Cloud KMS, BYOK/HSM via PKCS#11) and can provide sample key access logs on request.
- Audit & evidence: sample audit entries and the egress policy matrix included.

Attachments included here: redwood_isolation_narrative_v1.pdf (narrative + boundary table), netdiag_dedicated_private_v3.png (diagram), egress_policy_matrix.csv (egress controls per region).

Next steps:
1) I'll share these files now for your review.
2) Karthik will add a short HSM/KMS integration note and a sanitized sample audit log.
3) We can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough if you'd like us to talk through diagrams and answer SIG questions live.

If you want an executive-friendly 1-paragraph summary for your board packet, say the word and we'll produce it.

Marcus

Marcus / Irene —

Adding a few technical notes to supplement Marcus' narrative before we send the sanitized package to Solstice. I'll attach the KMS/HSM integration notes and a short checklist we use for Dedicated handoffs. Please redact any internal IP ranges or hostnames from the diagram image (netdiag_dedicated_private_v3.png) before final delivery — use placeholder CIDRs instead.

Technical details to include in the narrative (suggested wording):
- Control plane partitioning: control plane services run in a logically separate management tenancy; control messages use mutual TLS with short-lived certs; we rotate certs via an automated CA and log rotations to our audit stream.
- mTLS + identity: node/agent identity is managed via SPIFFE-compatible attestation; workload tokens are scoped with least privilege.
- KV cache isolation: the prefix/KV cache is namespace isolated; for Dedicated customers we have an option to dedicate cache instances per-tenant to eliminate cross-tenant memory channels.
- Egress handling: egress is routed through regional NATs with FQDN allowlists; customers can opt for a forced egress proxy hosted in their VPC. The egress_policy_matrix.csv includes the default and opt-in patterns.
- KMS/HSM: We support Cloud KMS integrations and on-prem HSMs via PKCS#11 gateway. When customers choose BYOK with HSM-backed keys we provide an audit log snippet format (redacted) showing cryptographic operations.

Attachments added: kms_hsm_integration_notes.txt (internal notes for redaction), please incorporate as a sanitized appendix if useful.

I'll prep a one-paragraph executive summary for Emma as well. Marcus — can you confirm redaction and push the sanitized artifacts to the shared link?

Thanks,
Karthik
